# Sector Brief — COST (Costco Wholesale)
**Sector:** Consumer Defensive — Discount Stores (US)
**Comp Set:** WMT (Walmart), TGT (Target) — same GICS industry; sector aggregates also mix in CPG (KO, PG, PEP, PM).

## 1. Sector Overview
US discount retail is a **mature, high-volume, low-margin** industry anchored by three scale players: Walmart (~$713B FY26 revenue), Costco (~$303B FY26), and Target (~$105B FY26). The channel is firmly in the late/mature stage of the cycle — revenue growth is single-digit at best and now bifurcating sharply: value/warehouse formats (COST, WMT) are taking share from general-merchandise chains, while Target is in outright revenue decline three straight years. The 2025–26 macro backdrop (tariff-driven cost inflation, soft US retail sales, cautious consumer) is concentrating trips in the highest-value formats.

## 2. Key Tailwinds
- **Trade-down / value-seeking consumer:** Affordability is the 2026 retail theme; warehouse clubs and discounters capture share when wallets tighten, supporting traffic and high membership renewal rates.
- **Membership fee flywheel:** Fees are near-pure profit and keep rising — Costco's fee revenue grew ~7.5% YoY to $1.33B in its August quarter after fee hikes (Gold Star → $65, Executive → $130). Every hike drops largely to the bottom line.
- **Private-label penetration & scale buying:** Kirkland Signature and club-scale procurement give COST/WMT pricing power against suppliers and insulation from branded-goods inflation.

## 3. Key Headwinds
- **Tariff-driven merchandise cost inflation:** Costco specifically missed profit targets on tariff costs in a recent quarter; Walmart has warned tariffs will pressure US prices. Input-cost passthrough is constrained at the low-margin end of retail.
- **Soft consumer spending:** US retail sales are slowing as tariffs and a cooling labour market hit confidence; economists expect the softness to persist — a cap on comp-sales growth across the sector.
- **Mature, saturated market:** North American club/box space is built-out; growth rides on ~20–25 new units/year, comps, and international execution (China/Asia ramp) — all lower-return than the historical US build-out.

## 4. Peer Comparison (latest completed fiscal years)

| Metric (latest FY) | **COST** (FY Aug-26) | **WMT** (FY Jan-26) | **TGT** (FY Jan-26) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $303.2B | $713.2B | $104.8B |
| Revenue growth (latest FY) | **+10.1%** | +4.7% | **−1.7%** |
| Revenue CAGR (5-yr) | **+9.1%** | +5.0% | +2.3% |
| Gross margin | 12.8% | 24.9% | 27.9% |
| Operating margin | 3.85% | 4.18% | 4.88% |
| OM trend (5-yr) | **Rising every year** (3.35%→3.85%) | Flat (~4.2%) | **Collapsed** (8.4%→4.9%) |
| Market cap | ~$408B | ~$830B | ~$71B |

*(COST's low gross margin is structural — a pass-through, low-margin-merchandise model whose profit engine is membership fees, which sit between gross and operating profit. FY dates differ by ~5 months across the three; comparable windows.)*

## 5. Target Company's Competitive Position — **STRONG**
COST is the standout operator in the comp set: it is the **only one growing revenue at a double-digit rate** (10.1% vs WMT +4.7%, TGT −1.7%) while its operating margin has **improved in five consecutive years** — evidence that membership-fee leverage + scale are compounding. WMT is a formidable, steady share-holder; TGT is actively losing market share with three straight down years and a halved operating margin. COST's membership model creates switching costs and recurring revenue most retailers lack, and its premium valuation (≈44× trailing EPS, roughly 2× the market) reflects that quality. Risks are concentrated in valuation and tariff passthrough, not in competitive position.

## 6. Sector Rating: **Neutral**
Discount retail is defensive but mature — structurally low-margin, price-transparent, and intensely competitive (Walmart, Target, Amazon, TJX), with tariff and demand headwinds in 2026. Within that neutral sector, however, the **warehouse-club/value sub-channel is attractive**: Costco and Walmart are gaining share from weaker peers, and cost pressure favours the strongest operators. Bottom line: the sector offers limited beta, but COST's idiosyncratic model (membership rents + double-digit growth) is the sector's best-positioned asset.

# COST (Costco Wholesale) — Geopolitical & Legal Risk Assessment

**Scope:** Geographic revenue map, geopolitical risks, litigation/regulatory exposure, compliance flags. Data reflects FY2025–FY2026 filings, company releases, court records and press reporting as of the research date.

---

## 1. Geographic Risk Map

Costco's ~$275B FY2025 net sales split (~73% US, ~13% Canada, ~14% "Other International," which combines Mexico and all other markets — Costco does not break out Mexico separately in 10-K geography tables):

| Country / Region | Est. revenue exposure | Warehouse count (latest) | Risk level | Key risk drivers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| United States / Puerto Rico | ~73% (~$200B) | ~650 | **Low-Med** | Active litigation & federal antitrust probes; stable rule of law |
| Canada | ~13% (~$37B) | ~110 | **Low** | USMCA renegotiation, tariff/counter-tariff friction |
| Mexico (largest "other intl" market) | ~7% (~$19B est.) | ~40 | **Medium-High** | US-Mexico tariff threats, peso volatility, supply-chain/crime risk |
| Japan | ~2% | ~30 | **Low-Med** | Demographics, yen volatility |
| UK | ~2% | ~30 | **Low** | CMA/regulatory, food-safety litigation contagion |
| South Korea | ~1.5% | ~16 | **Low-Med** | Regional security (DPRK), currency |
| Taiwan | ~1.5–2% | 14 | **High** | Strait conflict risk; operated as **non-controlling JV** — net income excluded from reported results (per 10-Q) |
| Australia, Spain, France, Iceland | ~2% combined | ~16 | **Low** | Immaterial exposure |
| **China** | <1% but strategic growth market | 7–8 stores (opened 2019–2026, incl. Shanghai/Shenzhen) | **High** | US-China tariff regime, PRC regulatory/consumer-pressures, export-control spillover |

**Structural note:** Costco's China exposure is two-sided — a small growing retail footprint *and* a very large import base (Chinese-sourced merchandise is a key cost input), which is what drags it into tariff litigation.

---

## 2. Top 3 Geopolitical Risks

1. **US-China tariff escalation (import-cost shock).** *Probability: High. Impact: Medium-High.* Costco sued the Trump administration seeking a "full refund" of Section 232 and Section 301 duties (NBC News, BBC) and has already recovered ~$184M in refunds after courts ruled companies are entitled to refunds on unlawfully imposed tariffs (Yahoo Finance). It simultaneously faces customer class actions (e.g., Stockov v. Costco) seeking a share of up to ~$170B in aggregate refunds (Reuters, 3/2026) on claims costco "illegally" raised prices. New tariff rounds would hit gross margins and pricing optics directly.

2. **Taiwan Strait conflict / PRC retaliation.** *Probability: Low. Impact: High.* 14 Taiwan warehouses (~2% of sales) sit in the highest-risk geopolitical theater; Taiwan income is deliberately quarantined as a non-controlling interest, signaling Costco itself treats it as contingent. A blockade or conflict would also sever regional logistics (Taiwan/China/Southeast Asia sourcing) well beyond the retail P&L.

3. **North America trade renegotiation (US- Mexico-Canada).** *Probability: Medium. Impact: Medium.* Canada (~13% of sales) and Mexico (~7%) make ~20% of revenue hostage to USMCA 2026 renegotiation, steel/aluminum tariff spillovers, and counter-tariffs (Costco's October sales comps already show Canada growth lagging the US — Globe and Mail). Peso/CAD currency swings compound margin pressure on imported goods.

---

## 3. Legal & Regulatory Highlights

- **Tariff refund litigation (both sides):** Plaintiff against the administration for 232/301 refunds (received $184M; case tied to SCOTUS review — BBC) **and** defendant in consumer "share of refunds" class actions (Reuters).
- **DOJ / state antitrust probes — food pricing:** DOJ opened an egg-price antitrust probe (Bloomberg, 3/2025); three major egg suppliers were subsequently charged and settled with DOJ + 17 states (2026); the beef-price investigation has been **expanded to Costco, Walmart and Amazon** (reported). Retailer-side exposure remains under investigation.
- **Employment litigation:** $8M settlement of California sex-bias class action (Law360); $200K jury award in disability discrimination case; active NLRB unfair-labor charge (Case 07-CA-383757); $868K worker-misclassification penalty (delivery affiliates).
- **Product liability / food safety:** Salmonella class actions tied to Nebraska processing plant (Yahoo Finance); PFAS "baby wipes" class action allowed to proceed on deceptive-marketing claims; LA-class Protein powder heavy-metals (Prop 65) suit; ~1M-bottle Prosecco recall on laceration risk (CPSC). These are recurring, quantifiable but manageable exposures for a staple-goods retailer.
- **Privacy:** Suit alleging Costco's pharmacy site leaked consumers' medical data to Meta via tracking pixels — a growing state-privacy-law (and potential HIPAA-adjacent) exposure class.
- **Political/regulatory pressure:** Multistate Republican AG letter (led by Texas) challenging Costco's DEI policies; shareholders rejected the anti-DEI proposal 98%–2% (NPR), but political pressure is ongoing.

---

## 4. Compliance Red Flags

- **Antitrust scrutiny of food pricing:** DOJ/state probes into egg and beef pricing name retailers; Costco's size makes it a litigation magnet regardless of merit.
- **Health-data privacy:** pharmacy tracking-pixel claims could trigger state AG/consumer-privacy actions and reputational damage.
- **Prop 65 / consumer-protection class actions:** recurring California exposure on heavy metals, PFAS, and promotional claims.
- **Customs valuation & tariff compliance:** active disputes over 232/301 duties invite CBP scrutiny of its import declarations.
- **FCPA/AML/sanctions:** No Russia/Iran/North Korea/Cuba operations and no known FCPA enforcement — genuinely low exposure here; China and Mexico operations are the jurisdictions to watch for corruption/AML risk, but no public allegations found.
- **Foreign-exchange/transfer controls:** repatriation of China and Mexico earnings is subject to local capital controls — immaterial today given scale.

---

## 5. Overall Geopolitical/Legal Risk Rating: **MEDIUM** (tilt toward Medium-High)
